english: you did it!; way to go
use: Congratulates a friend on a success; yatta alone is your own win.

examplePolite.romaji: goukaku shita n desu ka? yarimashita ne!
examplePolite.ja: 合格したんですか？やりましたね！

use: Praise from a parent, coach, or boss to someone below them.

example.romaji: yoku yatta! zenbu hitori de yatta no?
example.ja: よくやった！全部一人でやったの？
example.english: Well done! You did it all by yourself?

examplePolite.romaji: yoku yarimashita ne. taihen datta deshou.
examplePolite.ja: よくやりましたね。大変だったでしょう。
examplePolite.english: Well done. That must have been tough.

notes: It talks down, so don't say it to a boss; use otsukaresama deshita instead.

english: lucky you; I'm jealous; that's nice
use: Wistful reaction to someone's good news or to something you wish you had.

example.ja: いいなあ、ハワイ行くの？
example.english: Lucky you, you're going to Hawaii?

examplePolite.romaji: ii desu ne, hawai ni iku n desu ka.
examplePolite.ja: いいですね、ハワイに行くんですか。
examplePolite.english: How nice, you're going to Hawaii?

notes: The polite ii desu ne loses the hint of envy.

use: Quick praise for a good move, shot, or idea, often in sports and games.

example.romaji: naisu! ima no shuuto, sugoi yo.
example.ja: ナイス！今のシュート、すごいよ。

examplePolite.romaji: naisu desu! ima no shuuto, sugokatta desu.
examplePolite.ja: ナイスです！今のシュート、すごかったです。

notes: Often joined to a noun: naisu aidia (nice idea), naisu shotto.

use: Approves of how something looks, feels, or is coming along.

example.romaji: un, ii kanji! sono mama tsuzukete.
example.ja: うん、いい感じ！そのまま続けて。
example.english: Yeah, looks good! Keep going like that.

examplePolite.romaji: ii kanji desu ne. sono mama tsuzukete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: いい感じですね。そのまま続けてください。
examplePolite.english: That's looking good. Please keep going.

notes: About a person it means likable: ii kanji no hito (a nice person).

use: Approves of something; with a shrug it pushes 'why not, go for it'.

example.romaji: ii jan, sono fuku. niau yo.
example.ja: いいじゃん、その服。似合うよ。

examplePolite.romaji: ii ja nai desu ka, sono fuku. niaimasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: いいじゃないですか、その服。似合いますよ。
examplePolite.english: That outfit's nice. It suits you.

notes: The 'why not' use: ii jan, ikou yo (come on, let's go).

use: Judges by looks or description, before you've tried it.

examplePolite.ja: この店、よさそうですね。

notes: Not ii sou: the 'looks' form of ii is irregular.

use: Excited when you find exactly what you wanted.

example.romaji: kore kore! kono aji ga tabetakatta.
example.ja: これこれ！この味が食べたかった。
example.english: This is it! This is the taste I've been craving.

examplePolite.romaji: kore kore! kono aji ga tabetakatta n desu.
examplePolite.ja: これこれ！この味が食べたかったんです。
examplePolite.english: This is it! This is the taste I wanted.

notes: From an older person to a child, it's a gentle 'now, now' scolding.

kana: おたんじょうびおめでとう
politeJa: お誕生日おめでとうございます
use: The answer is arigatou; add gozaimasu for anyone you speak politely to.

example.romaji: otanjoubi omedetou! kyou wa ogoru yo.
example.ja: お誕生日おめでとう！今日はおごるよ。

examplePolite.romaji: otanjoubi omedetou gozaimasu. kyou wa watashi ga ogorimasu.
examplePolite.ja: お誕生日おめでとうございます。今日は私がおごります。
examplePolite.english: Happy birthday. Today is my treat.

notes: Friends often shorten it to tanjoubi omedetou or just omedetou.

politeJa: ご結婚おめでとうございます
use: To a friend getting married; the polite form with go- is what goes on cards and at the reception.

example.ja: 結婚おめでとう！幸せにね。
example.english: Congrats on getting married! Be happy.

examplePolite.ja: ご結婚おめでとうございます。お幸せに。
examplePolite.english: Congratulations on your marriage. Wishing you every happiness.

politeJa: 合格おめでとうございます
use: For passing an entrance exam, a certification test, or an audition.

example.ja: 合格おめでとう！よく頑張ったね。
example.english: Congrats on passing! You worked so hard.

examplePolite.romaji: goukaku omedetou gozaimasu. yoku ganbarimashita ne.
examplePolite.ja: 合格おめでとうございます。よく頑張りましたね。
examplePolite.english: Congratulations on passing. You worked really hard.

kana: そつぎょうおめでとう
politeJa: ご卒業おめでとうございます
use: Heard most in March, Japan's graduation season.

example.romaji: sotsugyou omedetou! haru kara shakaijin da ne.
example.ja: 卒業おめでとう！春から社会人だね。
example.english: Congrats on graduating! You start working this spring.

examplePolite.romaji: gosotsugyou omedetou gozaimasu. haru kara oshigoto desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: ご卒業おめでとうございます。春からお仕事ですね。
examplePolite.english: Congratulations on graduating. You start work in spring, right?

english: that must have been hard; what an ordeal
use: Sympathy after someone tells you about a rough time; often followed by daijoubu?

example.romaji: sore wa taihen datta ne. mou daijoubu?
example.ja: それは大変だったね。もう大丈夫？
example.english: That must have been rough. Are you okay now?

examplePolite.romaji: sore wa taihen deshita ne. mou daijoubu desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: それは大変でしたね。もう大丈夫ですか？
examplePolite.english: That must have been hard. Are you all right now?

notes: For something still going on, say taihen da ne (that's tough).

english: that sounds really hard; that must hurt
use: Sympathy for emotional pain: a breakup, a loss, a painful situation.

example.romaji: wakareta no? sore wa tsurai ne.
example.ja: 別れたの？それはつらいね。
example.english: You broke up? That must really hurt.

examplePolite.romaji: wakareta n desu ka. sore wa tsurai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 別れたんですか。それはつらいですね。
examplePolite.english: You broke up? That must be hard.

notes: taihen is about hassle and effort; tsurai is about pain.

politeJa: 気を落とさないでください
english: don't let it get you down; don't lose heart
use: Comfort after a failure or disappointment, like a lost game or a rejection.

example.romaji: tsugi ga aru kara, ki o otosanaide.
example.ja: 次があるから、気を落とさないで。
example.english: There's always next time, don't let it get you down.

examplePolite.romaji: tsugi ga arimasu kara, ki o otosanaide kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 次がありますから、気を落とさないでください。
examplePolite.english: There will be a next time, so please don't lose heart.

notes: Friends often say ki ni shinaide (don't worry about it) instead.

politeJa: 焦らなくていいですよ
use: Reassures someone who is hurrying or panicking.

example.romaji: jikan aru kara, aseranakute ii yo.
example.ja: 時間あるから、焦らなくていいよ。
example.english: We've got time, no need to rush.

examplePolite.romaji: jikan wa arimasu kara, aseranakute ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 時間はありますから、焦らなくていいですよ。
examplePolite.english: There's time, so no need to rush.

notes: Built from aseru (to panic, rush) plus -nakute ii (you don't have to).

politeJa: 早く良くなってくださいね
use: To someone sick or injured, as you leave or end a call.

example.ja: 風邪？早く良くなってね。

examplePolite.romaji: hayaku yoku natte kudasai ne. odaiji ni.
examplePolite.ja: 早く良くなってくださいね。お大事に。

notes: odaiji ni (take care of yourself) is the standard set phrase to anyone unwell.

src: 風邪ひかないようにね
ja: 風邪ひかないようにね
kana: かぜひかないようにね
polite: kaze o hikanai you ni ki o tsukete kudasai
politeJa: 風邪をひかないように気をつけてください
english: don't catch a cold; stay warm
use: A caring send-off when it's cold or someone's heading out in the rain.

example.romaji: kyou samui kara, kaze hikanai you ni ne.
example.ja: 今日寒いから、風邪ひかないようにね。
example.english: It's cold today, so don't catch a cold.

examplePolite.romaji: kaze o hikanai you ni ki o tsukete kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: 風邪をひかないように気をつけてくださいね。
examplePolite.english: Be careful not to catch a cold.

notes: Catching a cold is kaze o hiku, literally 'pull a cold'.
